session_incident_tracking.overview: Critical instructions for maintaining incident context throughout a Bob session. This ensures proper tracking and allows multiple users to work independently on the same ServiceNow instance without conflicts.
session_incident_tracking.critical_rule: Once an incident is created in ServiceNow, you MUST maintain and reference that incident ID throughout the entire session until the incident is closed. This is NON-NEGOTIABLE and essential for proper incident management.

why_this_matters.reason: Maintains complete audit trail for a single incident
Prevents creating duplicate incidents for the same issue
Allows multiple users to run labs simultaneously on same ServiceNow instance
Ensures all work notes and updates are associated with correct incident
Provides clear incident lifecycle from creation to closure

step.action: Store incident identifier immediately after creation
step.details:
When create_incident succeeds, the response contains: - number: The incident number (e.g., "INC0010005") - sys_id: The internal ServiceNow identifier
You MUST store BOTH of these values in your session context.
step.example: After successful creation: "✅ Created incident INC0010005 (sys_id: abc123def456) for tracking this issue."

step.action: Reference stored incident ID for every ServiceNow operation

operations.operation: Always use the stored incident number or sys_id as the identifier parameter
All work notes must be added to the SAME incident
State changes (New → In Progress → Resolved) must be applied to the SAME incident
Final closure must be performed on the SAME incident

step.example: Throughout the session: "Updating incident INC0010005 with diagnosis findings..." "Updating incident INC0010005 with remediation plan..." "Updating incident INC0010005 with verification results..." "Closing incident INC0010005 as resolved..."

step.action: Display incident ID prominently in all status updates
step.details: Include the incident number in your communications so the user always knows which incident is being tracked. This provides transparency and helps users verify the correct incident is being updated.

examples.good: "Incident INC0010005: Diagnosis complete - server overload detected"

step.action: Never create multiple incidents for the same issue
step.details:
If you encounter an error updating an incident: 1. Troubleshoot the update operation 2. Verify the incident ID is correct 3. Check if incident still exists using get_incident 4. Retry the update operation 5. DO NOT create a new incident
Only create a new incident if: - User explicitly requests tracking a DIFFERENT issue - Previous incident was successfully closed and new issue reported

multi_user_support.principle: Each user's Bob session maintains its own incident context independently, allowing multiple users to run the lab simultaneously on the same ServiceNow instance without any conflicts or cross-contamination.

how_it_works.scenario:
User A starts a session: - Creates incident INC0010005 - Bob tracks INC0010005 throughout User A's entire session - All updates go to INC0010005
User B starts a separate session (same ServiceNow instance): - Creates incident INC0010006 - Bob tracks INC0010006 throughout User B's entire session - All updates go to INC0010006
Result: - No conflicts between users - Each incident has complete, independent lifecycle - ServiceNow shows two separate incidents with proper tracking

benefits.benefit: Multiple students can complete the lab simultaneously
Each student has their own incident to track
No confusion about which incident belongs to which user
Clean audit trail for each user's work

when_to_reference.timing: When displaying status updates to user
When documenting actions in work notes

session_context_management.session_lifetime: The incident context persists from creation until: - Incident is successfully closed (state = 6 or 7) - User explicitly starts working on a different incident - Session ends (user closes Bob or starts new conversation)

scenario.name: Lost incident context
scenario.detection: You realize you don't have the incident ID stored, or you're unsure which incident you should be updating.

resolution.step: Ask user: "Which incident number are you working with?"
If user doesn't know, use list_incidents to find recent incidents
Once identified, store that incident ID and use it going forward
Confirm with user: "I'll continue tracking incident INC0010005"

scenario.name: Update operation fails
scenario.detection: update_incident returns an error (e.g., "Incident not found", "Invalid state transition")

resolution.step: Verify the incident ID is correct (check what you have stored)
Use get_incident to check if incident still exists
If incident exists, analyze the error and fix the update parameters
Retry the update operation with corrected parameters
DO NOT create a new incident as a workaround

scenario.example: Error: "Invalid state transition from 6 to 2" Analysis: Incident is already resolved (state 6), can't move back to In Progress (state 2) Solution: Either reopen incident first, or acknowledge it's already resolved DO NOT: Create a new incident

scenario.name: User mentions different incident
scenario.detection: User says something like "What about incident INC0010007?" when you've been tracking INC0010005

resolution.step: Clarify with user which incident they want to work on
If switching to different incident, acknowledge the switch
Update your stored incident context to the new incident

practice.name: Always display incident number in communications
practice.rationale: Keeps user informed and prevents confusion
practice.example: "Updating incident INC0010005 with diagnosis: Server overload detected (CPU: 95%, Memory: 88%)"

practice.name: Store incident ID immediately after creation
practice.rationale: Prevents losing track of which incident to update
practice.implementation: As soon as create_incident succeeds, extract and store: - response.result.number - response.result.sys_id

practice.name: Reference incident ID in every update operation
practice.rationale: Ensures all updates go to correct incident
practice.implementation: Every update_incident call must include the stored incident identifier

practice.name: Verify incident exists before major operations
practice.rationale: Catches issues early before attempting updates
practice.when: - Before starting remediation phase - After any long-running operations - If you suspect the incident might have been modified externally

practice.name: Include incident number in todo list items
practice.example: [x] Create and track incident INC0010005 in ServiceNow [-] Diagnose root cause for INC0010005 [ ] Apply remediation for INC0010005

anti_pattern.issue: Creating multiple incidents for the same issue
anti_pattern.why_bad: - Fragments the audit trail - Confuses incident tracking - Makes it impossible to see complete incident lifecycle - Breaks multi-user lab scenario
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Create ONE incident at the start, track it throughout the entire session

anti_pattern.issue: Not displaying incident number in status updates
anti_pattern.why_bad: - User doesn't know which incident is being tracked - Hard to verify correct incident is being updated - Reduces transparency
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Always include incident number: "Updating incident INC0010005..."

anti_pattern.issue: Losing track of incident ID mid-session
anti_pattern.why_bad: - Can't update the incident - May create duplicate incident - Breaks incident lifecycle
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Store incident ID immediately after creation and reference it consistently

anti_pattern.issue: Using wrong incident ID for updates
anti_pattern.why_bad: - Updates go to wrong incident - Corrupts other users' incidents - Creates confusion in ServiceNow
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Always use the incident ID stored at creation time for YOUR session

verification_checklist.check: ✓ All updates go to same incident
✓ Closing the SAME incident that was created
✓ Complete lifecycle tracked in one incident

session_incident_tracking.summary:
Session-based incident tracking is CRITICAL for proper incident management.
Key principles: 1. ONE incident per issue per session 2. Store incident ID immediately after creation 3. Reference that ID in ALL subsequent operations 4. Display incident number in ALL communications 5. NEVER create duplicate incidents for same issue
This approach ensures: - Complete audit trail - Multi-user lab support - Clear incident lifecycle - Professional incident management
